content:
The image shows a seedling at soil level with:
- Very early emergence stage (cotyledons just emerging)
- Brown to dark brown rotted roots visible — the root tissue appears decayed and discolored
- The hypocotyl/root area shows decay and discoloration extending from the soil line
- Soil is wet/saturated (dark, muddy conditions)
- Plant appears collapsed or struggling to emerge

Key observations:
- Wet soil conditions favoring water molds
- Rotted root system visible — dark, brown, decayed roots
- Seedling appears in pre- or post-emergence damping off state
- No reddish-brown sunken firm cankers (rules out Rhizoctonia)
- Soft, water-soaked rot in wet conditions points to Pythium

This matches **Pythium_damping_off**: water-soaked soft rot of roots/hypocotyl in wet soil conditions, with rotted roots allowing easy pulling from soil, at the seedling emergence stage.

Rhizoctonia would show firm, dry, reddish-brown sunken lesions — not soft wet rot. Phytophthora typically shows chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward. The wet soil + soft rot pattern at emergence is most consistent with Pythium.
